text:
sara: FYI KaleHealth is hitting p95 tail timeouts (504) for hosted inference since ~11:10 UTC. Customer reports timeouts on their nightly batch, ~30% requests 504.
ops-bot: ALERT: route=kv-hosted-prod KaleHealth spike detected (queue_depth=98/100, continuous_batch_backlog=42). Pager oncall: @mike
mike: grabbing traces. can someone drop example trace ids + a repro request?
anita: sending logs from support — customer provided trace id: trace=kh-4fb2-9a. They repro with curl to our api: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-3-small","input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` 
sara: attaching snippet from their logs: `gateway: request_queue_depth=99 enqueue_ts=1700000000 dequeue_ts=1700000300 deadline_exceeded`
lee: looks like continuous-batcher backlog + enqueue hold. queue depth close to 100 limit. could be a tenant hotspot + longseq pushing KV cache misses. any recent deploys to batching runtime?
mike: no deploys in last hour. metric spike started at 11:09. I've started a trace dump for the host group.
anita: customer says batch size is large (avg tokens ~1200). they ramped up concurrent jobs overnight.
lee: immediate mitigation options: 1) lower route max_inflight for KaleHealth to 20, 2) enable fallback to smaller model variant, 3) temporarily increase queue depth limit (risky). prefer 1+2.
mike: i'm reducing route concurrency now: `redwoodctl routes update --tenant kalehealth --route default --max-inflight 20`
deploy-bot: action started by mike: route update job id=job-8821
mike: update returned success. monitoring for next 2 min.
sara: customer still seeing 504s but reduced frequency. p95 dropped from 6.8s -> 3.2s.
lee: good. next we should check continuous batcher backlog eviction rate and KV miss ratio. jason can you pull kvcache metrics for tenant?
jason: pulling kvcache_hit_ratio, eviction_rate, avg_batch_latency for kalehealth... kvcache_hit_ratio=0.42, eviction_rate=18/s, avg_batch_latency=220ms. eviction spikes line up with the tail timeouts.
anm: (typo) sorry ignore
lee: low hit ratio + eviction rate suggests repeated long sequences causing cold KV spins, increasing batcher backlog. propose adding a small prefix cache for their tenant and recommending they shard their nightly jobs.
anita: customer asked if this is billing/auth related — it's not. Auth logs show no errors for their keys.
mike: opening ENG ticket for runtime-level fixes (priority P1). Ticket: ENG-9483. adding traces and metrics.
mike: also enabling per-tenant fallback to redwood-3-tiny for requests that exceed token threshold: `redwoodctl routes update --tenant kalehealth --route default --fallback-model redwood-3-tiny --fallback-token-threshold 1024`
deploy-bot: action started by mike: route update job id=job-8822
sara: after fallback enabled p95 further improved to 1.8s, customer says batch job completed with retries.
lee: short-term mitigation successful. For next steps: S1) add runaway longseq detection and early-fallback at the gateway, S2) add tenant-level KV warmup hinting, S3) review queue_depth soft-limit behavior to avoid abrupt rejections.
anita: i've informed KaleHealth support lead and shared the workaround. they're ok with sharding nightly runs for now.
mike: leaving note to escalate to product for safer queue depth knobs and better telemetry on per-route enqueue latencies.
jason: saving graphs and traces to ENG-9483, will attach KV heatmaps.
mike: closing incident thread after follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark: 
sara: thanks team. will schedule postmortem check-in tomorrow 15:00 UTC. :eyes:
